disease.name: Pink Bollworm
disease.severity_index: Can cause up to 30–50% yield loss if untreated

environmental_factors.soil_conditions: More prevalent in irrigated cotton fields

region_specific_information.Andhra Pradesh: Severe outbreaks in regions with continuous cotton cropping
region_specific_information.Telangana: Higher infestation in Bt cotton-growing areas

early_stage: Small boreholes on young cotton bolls
mid_stage: Larvae inside bolls feeding on seeds
Discolored lint due to pest damage
advanced_stage: Poor fiber quality leading to economic loss

crop_rotation: Rotate with non-host crops like pulses
Plow fields after harvest to expose and kill larvae
soil_seed_treatment: Seed treatment with Imidacloprid 70 WS @ 5 g/kg seed to prevent early attacks

cultural_practices: Destroy infested bolls to prevent larvae carryover
Use pheromone traps (at 5 traps/acre) to monitor adult moth activity
Practice deep plowing after harvest to expose larvae
Early sowing to escape peak pest infestation
biological_control: Release of Trichogramma bactrae (egg parasitoid) for natural control
Spraying Neem Oil @ 5 ml/L water to deter egg-laying
